35.0.s.en: (1) Taking refuge in the mighty Defender

35.0.0.en: 1- Plead my cause, O LORD, with them that strive with me: fight against them that fight against me.

35.0.1.en: 1- David asks God to stand as an adversary against his enemies. David feels the strength of the enemies and his own personal weakness, but he trusts in God's power as a fighter and adversary, so that He frightens the enemies and drives them away from David.

35.0.2.en: 2- David's enemy was King Saul with all his power and authority, so David had nothing to do but take refuge in One who is stronger than the king, and he took refuge in God, the King of kings. Our enemy is Satan, and our war is with the spiritual hosts of wickedness; therefore we take refuge in God, who is stronger than all.

35.0.3.en: 3- David did not ask for vengeance on his enemies, but asked only - in his refuge in God - that God stand before him and protect him from the enemies. He does not want the death of the enemies, but that God defend him.

35.1.0.en: 2- Take hold of shield and buckler, and stand up for mine help.

35.1.2.en: Buckler: a defensive instrument that the soldier held in ancient times to defend himself. It is a rectangular piece of wood with a loop at the back, in which the soldier puts his hand and moves it in front of his head and body, to ward off the enemy's arrows with it.

35.1.3.en: 1- David asks God to go out to war before him, holding a shield and buckler to protect him from the arrows; he wants to hide behind God, and he believes that God's power is able to repel everything from him.

35.1.4.en: 2- He asks God to stand up; and God, of course, is not a man who carries something or rises from place to place, but David means that God should show His power, so that the enemies are afraid. That is, He should frighten the enemies in any way, whether by David or by any other person, and turn the enemies away from him, so that David suffers no harm.

35.1.5.en: 3- What is meant by the buckler is the shield of faith, that is, David's faith in God, so that he is not alarmed by the strength of the enemies, and then God will repel them from him. The weapons are spiritual and not material, and the shield is God Himself, not a material instrument.

35.2.0.en: 3- Draw out also the spear, and stop the way against them that persecute me: say unto my soul, I am thy salvation.

35.2.1.en: Draw out: bring out and aim the spear.

35.2.2.en: 1- David asks God to ready His spear to frighten his enemies, and God does not use the spears known among men, but David means the word of God, which exposes the demons, conquers them and frightens them.

35.2.3.en: 2- David also asked God to stop his pursuers, and did not ask for vengeance on them, for he needs God's protection and loves his enemies. Saul fell twice into David's hand, and he let him go and did not harm him, so David is an example of love for enemies.

35.2.4.en: 3- David also asked God to say to him that He is his Savior. He did not ask to obtain salvation, but to hear a word from God, because he believes that the word of God is effective and powerful and must be fulfilled at the proper time. This is evidence of David's faith and reliance on God.

35.2.5.en: 4- David was exposed to many pursuers, the first of whom was Saul, who pursued him for many years and kept pursuing him until Saul died in the war. Likewise the Edomites, the descendants of Esau, used to raid him and fight him, since they lived south of his country, and pursued him, but God used to strengthen him and protect him from them, and even to defeat them before him. Likewise his son Absalom drove him from his throne and tried to kill him. In addition to all the peoples who tried to oppose and pursue him, and also Abner, the commander of Saul's army, who fought him for seven years and afterward was reconciled with him. David was exposed to many pursuers.

35.2.6.en: 5- When did God need a spear to fight with? Only when He needed a body in order to redeem us. This is a symbol of the Incarnation of God in the fullness of time, to save us and die for us on the Cross, and to repel from us the wars of the devil, who pursues us to make us fall into his snares.

35.3.0.en: 4- Let them be confounded and put to shame that seek after my soul: let them be turned back and brought to confusion that devise my hurt.

35.3.1.en: 1- Because of David's steadfastness in faith, relying on God, his enemies fear him and feel shame because of their weakness and inability to oppose him. These words apply to those who were enemies of David on earth, or to the demons who were fighting him.

35.3.2.en: 2- David also asks that his enemies draw back because of their feeling of weakness before him. All this is based on the appearance of God's power in him to the degree that it frightens the enemies. David does not want to gloat over his enemies, but that God's power appear and be glorified.

35.3.3.en: 3- This verse applies to Christ on the Cross, and at the hour of His arrest, for He asks for the shame of the wicked who oppose Him. Satan was put to shame when Christ bound him by His death on the Cross, and likewise when the Jews tried to arrest Him in the garden of Gethsemane, and He said to them "I am He," and they were afraid, went backward and fell to the ground (Jn 18:6).

35.4.0.en: 5- Let them be as chaff before the wind: and let the angel of the LORD chase them.

35.4.1.en: Chaff: a dry leaf of a plant that the wind can carry because of its lightness.

35.4.2.en: Chase them: pursue them and defeat those who pursued him.

35.4.3.en: 1- David asks that his pursuers be like chaff before the wind, that is, that their extreme weakness before the power of God appear. The wind signifies the Holy Spirit, and the chaff signifies extreme weakness, that is, that they become as nothing, and in the Hebrew original "splendor."

35.4.4.en: 2- The angel of God shows the power of God, who is able to defeat all the power of men, as the power of God appeared in the angel who killed 185,000 of the army of Sennacherib (2 Chr 32:21), and as the angels surrounded Judas Maccabeus to protect him from the arrows of the enemies, and he defeated them (2 Macc 11:6-8).

35.4.5.en: 3- The angel who defeats the enemies of the children of God is Christ, as He is called the angel of the covenant (Mal 3:1); it is He who defeated the devil and bound him by the Cross.

35.5.0.en: 6- Let their way be dark and slippery: and let the angel of the LORD persecute them.

35.5.1.en: Slippery: a road on which the one walking on it slips easily.

35.5.2.en: 1- To show the seriousness of evil, David asks that the way of his pursuers be dark and slippery, so that they cannot see the road, and fall in it, and do not reach their goal, which is to harm the children of God. Here too he does not want vengeance on them, but to hinder them from doing evil. This happened in the plague of darkness upon the Egyptians in the days of Moses (Ex 10:22), and in the angel of the Lord who appeared in the form of a pillar of fire and troubled Pharaoh's army at the Red Sea; but Pharaoh insisted on following the children of Israel, so he and all his army were drowned (Ex 14:19, 24).

35.5.3.en: 2- When the angel of God chases David's pursuers, he prevents them from carrying out their evils, and shows them the power of God, that perhaps they may repent; so David asks for the salvation of their souls and at the same time for his protection from their evils.

35.6.0.en: 7- For without cause have they hid for me their net in a pit, which without cause they have digged for my soul.

35.6.1.en: 8- Let destruction come upon him at unawares; and let his net that he hath hid catch himself: into that very destruction let him fall.

35.6.3.en: 1- The wicked do evil and wrong the righteous without any cause, that is, the righteous have done nothing to wrong them, but because the nature of the wicked is evil, they incline to evil in all their dealings, and wrong others without cause, and therefore their punishment from God is great.

35.6.4.en: 2- The wicked are hypocrites; they show affection to the righteous, then hide for them plots and calamities to make them fall into them. This confirms their malice and evil.

35.6.5.en: 3- God intervenes and turns the evil so that it comes upon the head of the wicked man who prepares the traps by digging pits and covering them with nets so that the righteous fall into them, but the wicked forget the places of these pits and fall into them themselves. And God turns the evil so that it does not strike the righteous but comes upon the wicked, as Ahithophel tried by his counsel to kill David, though he had formerly been David's counselor; but when Absalom rejected Ahithophel's counsel he was greatly vexed and hanged himself, and died (2 Sam 17:23), while David was kept by God, and neither Absalom nor Ahithophel harmed him. Likewise Absalom tried to kill his father, and he was killed and David escaped (2 Sam 18:15). And Judas Iscariot betrayed Christ to die and then hanged himself (Mt 27:5) and perished, while Christ, after He accomplished redemption on the Cross, rose from the dead. And Satan wanted to kill Christ and bind Him on the Cross, but was surprised that Christ bound him by His death on the Cross, and abolished his authority over the children of God.

35.6.6.en: 4- Just as the wicked man prepares a hidden plot for the destruction of the righteous, so he too is destroyed without knowing it, while the Lord delivers the righteous.

35.6.7.en: 5- The nature of the wicked is to do evil, and the nature of the righteous is to do good; therefore evil comes upon the head of the wicked, and good comes upon the head of the righteous, that is, every person's work returns upon him; perhaps this is a warning to all people, that they may repent of their sins and do good.

35.7.0.en: 9- And my soul shall be joyful in the LORD: it shall rejoice in his salvation.

35.7.1.en: 10- All my bones shall say, LORD, who is like unto thee, which deliverest the poor from him that is too strong for him, yea, the poor and the needy from him that spoileth him?

35.7.2.en: 1- The joy of the children of God is in God Himself, and not because He delivered them from the enemy's plots; or it is joy and occupation with God who delivered them, that is, occupation with His Person more than with anything else.

35.7.3.en: 2- The bones represent the inside, that is, man's heart thanks God, and not only his tongue; all of man's members, his feelings, and every pulse within him thank God.

35.7.4.en: 3- The children of God see the wonderful works of God that surpass the mind, so they say to Him, "Who is like unto thee," that is, no one can be found who loves us like You and cares for all the details of our life. God's love was perfected in His death on the Cross for us; this is the greatest love, the like of which is not in the whole earth, and perhaps David, in the spirit of prophecy, saw the redemption of Christ and said, "O God, who is like unto thee."

35.7.5.en: 4- When God intervenes to rescue the poor man, who is the poor and weak one, from the one who dominates him, robs him and exploits him, the poor man feels that he is stronger than all the strong of the world by God's support of him, so he thanks Him and says to Him, "Who is like unto thee." Perhaps this poor and needy man is David, who suffered much from Saul's pursuit of him, where Saul used his authority as king in pursuing David, but God delivered him.

35.7.6.en: Be at peace as long as God is with you, however much the wicked surround you and threaten you, and even if they are able to wrong you, God will compensate you and lift you up, while they will perish.

35.8.0.en: 11- False witnesses rise up; they ask me of things that I knew not.

35.8.1.en: 12- They reward me evil for good to the bereaving of my soul.

35.8.2.en: Bereaving: loss, or deprivation of children, and here it means humiliation.

35.8.3.en: 1- The servants of Saul rose up and informed against David to King Saul, and questioned him and investigated him concerning what they accused him of, though they were all false accusations, and David tried to convince Saul of his innocence and not to listen to these false witnesses, but Saul in his wickedness continued to pursue David.

35.8.4.en: 2- False witnesses rose up against Christ, and the high priest investigated Him, and could not find any fault in Him.

35.8.5.en: 3- Saul repaid David evil instead of his good; for David used to play music for Saul so that he would be calmed when the evil spirit came upon him, but instead of thanking him, Saul rose up to pursue him and try to kill him. Saul fell twice into David's hand, and he did not harm him, and Saul confessed to David that he was more righteous than he, and said to David, "Thou art more righteous than I: for thou hast rewarded me good, whereas I have rewarded thee evil" (1 Sam 24:17).

35.8.6.en: 4- David's enemies tried to make his soul bereaved, that is, without children, meaning to humiliate him, kill him, and blot out his name and any offspring of his; but God delivered David, and he lived and reigned over the children of Israel, and even became an example of godliness and righteousness, and from his seed came Christ.

35.8.7.en: 5- The Jews tried to kill Christ and blot out His name, but He rose from the dead, and the Apostles preached Him in the whole world.

35.8.8.en: 6- Perhaps David saw in the spirit of prophecy Christ, who went about everywhere doing good, and the Jews rose up against Him and demanded His crucifixion, and even crucified Him, and repaid Him evil for good.

35.9.0.en: 13- But as for me, when they were sick, my clothing was sackcloth: I humbled my soul with fasting; and my prayer returned into mine own bosom.

35.9.1.en: 1- Although David's enemies tried to kill him, he had done them much good. When they were sick, or in affliction, he prayed and humbled himself for them, and even put on sackcloth, which is rough clothing for humbling oneself before God, and fasted that God might intervene and have mercy on them; perhaps this happened when Saul was afflicted with an evil spirit that came upon him, and David served him to give him rest.

35.9.2.en: 2- David prayed for his enemies, but his prayer returned to his bosom, that is, God rejoiced in David's prayer and blessed him with good, but did not answer his prayer because of the evil of his enemies.

35.9.3.en: 3- The return of the prayer to David's bosom moved his heart to pray again, and so he lived in what is called constant prayer, so that he said of himself, "but I give myself unto prayer" (Ps 109:4).

35.9.4.en: 4- Christ prayed for those who crucified Him while on the Cross, that God would forgive them, but they did not benefit, because of their persistence in evil and unbelief.

35.10.0.en: 14- I behaved myself as though he had been my friend or brother: I bowed down heavily, as one that mourneth for his mother.

35.10.1.en: 1- David continues to explain his feelings toward his enemies whom he loved, and sympathized with in their afflictions and sicknesses; he says that he counted his enemy as his relative or his brother, so he felt his pains, was moved by his sufferings, and prayed for him with all his heart.

35.10.2.en: 2- David's feelings toward his enemy increased, so he counted him as his mother, because the relation of a son to his mother is one of the strongest relations. So he used to weep for his enemy in many prayers and was moved by his condition, like a person weeping over the loss of his mother.

35.10.3.en: 3- David also expresses his sorrows for his enemy, saying that he bowed down with grief, that is, he no longer looked at food and drink and clothing and all the adornment of the world. Indeed his sorrows increased, so he wept and bowed toward the ground, because he was moved by his enemy's suffering. These feelings show the extent of his love for every person, even one who is hostile to him.

35.10.4.en: 4- Christ wept over Jerusalem, which He knew would rise up against Him and crucify Him; so despite the Jews' enmity toward Him He loved them, and wept over them and counted them His brethren (Mk 3:35). David, in his grief for his enemy, signifies Christ's grief over Jerusalem (Mt 23:37).

35.11.0.en: 15- But in my halting they rejoiced and gathered together; they gathered together against me, reviling, and I knew it not; they tore and ceased not.

35.11.2.en: 1- David's love grows greater toward his enemies, because they wronged him greatly. When David was suffering his heavy pains he would groan as though limping from their weight; sadly, they gloated over him and rejoiced in his weariness, and this shows that their hearts were filled with evil.

35.11.3.en: 2- David's enemies gathered against him and conspired to wrong him, which is a persistence on their part in evil and a cooperation in wronging him.

35.11.4.en: 3- David's enemies were not content with wronging him in their hearts by rejoicing at his troubles, but went further in their evil, and reviled him when they gathered in his absence, and David did not know at the time, but he learned afterward.

35.11.5.en: 4- David's enemies went still further in their evil, and committed greater wrongs, "they tore," that is, they wronged him and harmed him and continued to harm him, and this means the absence of any pity for David.

35.11.6.en: 5- All that happened with David was a symbol of what happened with Christ when the Jews gloated over Him during His sufferings; they scourged Him, divided His garments, crucified Him naked, and rejoiced at His calamity, while Christ loved them and died for their salvation.

35.12.0.en: 16- Among the profane mockers for the sake of a cake they gnashed upon me with their teeth.

35.12.1.en: Mockers: plural of a jester, who is one who jokes and scoffs with little shame.

35.12.2.en: Gnashed with their teeth: ground their teeth (gnashed upon them) out of rage.

35.12.3.en: 1- David shows that his enemies are wicked, going further in their evils, for they wronged him without limits; and he endured for God's sake, because he was innocent, that is, he was wronged and endured.

35.12.4.en: 2- These enemies also mocked him without manners, and directed hard words at him that increased his pains, and he endured and remained holding fast to his faith.

35.12.5.en: 3- These wicked also persisted in their evils and harbored evil toward him, and when the opportunity did not come to them to carry out their wrongs they would be enraged and grind their teeth, and David did not fear them and stood firm in his faith.

35.12.6.en: 4- When God did good to David, providing for him, for example, his needs of food and drink, even if it was little, which is symbolized by a cake, this enraged his enemies, so they gnashed their teeth upon him, since they wanted David to die of hunger and want.

35.12.7.en: 5- What David's enemies did to him was a symbol of what happened with Christ, when the Jews and the Gentiles rose up against Him and wronged Him, and wanted to kill Him, and in the end crucified Him.

35.12.8.en: When you meet injustice, or wrongs from others, know that your Christ endured more than this for you, and He feels with you and is able to deliver you, so be at peace and ask for His help, and He will support you and comfort you.

35.13.0.en: 17- LORD, how long wilt thou look on? restore my soul from their destructions, my only one from the young lions.

35.13.1.en: 1- David reproaches God and says to Him, why do You look on, that is, watch and see Your son David suffering and being fought by the enemies, and You are silent despite the abundance of the wicked's injustice? He calls to Him to intervene and rescue him from the hands of the wicked. This shows David's faith in God and his boldness with Him.

35.13.2.en: 2- David asks God to restore his soul from the destructions of the wicked, because David beholds every day death and destruction at the hands of the wicked, so he is as good as dead; therefore he asks God to restore his soul, that is, to give him life and bring him out of their hands, and keep them away from him, that he may live and glorify God.

35.13.3.en: 3- David feels that he has one soul that he wants to live for God, and he fears for it from the cruelty of the enemies, whom he likens to wild animals, namely the young lions, which also signify the demons, so he asks God to rescue his soul from all evil, that he may stand firm in his faith and his life with God.

35.13.4.en: 4- This verse is a prophecy about Christ, against whom the Jews rose up and whom they tried to kill many times, so He asks the Father to rescue His only one, that is, His soul that is different from the rest of the souls; for after He died on the Cross, Satan tried to seize His soul, but was surprised that Christ had seized him and bound him so that he would not harm His children for whom He died. And Christ descended to Hades and brought up Adam and his sons to Paradise. Christ alone is able to overcome Satan and deliver His children from him, and the Father preserved His soul because the divinity is united with the human spirit, so He descended to Hades and ascended with His children who believe in Him.

35.14.0.en: 18- I will give thee thanks in the great congregation: I will praise thee among much people.

35.14.1.en: 1- David feels his oneness with the rest of the believers of the people of God, so he praises God and thanks Him with the rest of his people, and this establishes and builds up his faith, because communal praise strengthens the soul.

35.14.2.en: 2- Any blessing that one of the people of God receives gladdens the rest of the people, because they are all members of one body, which is the Church, and when one praises, the whole congregation rejoices; thanksgiving from one affects the rest and gladdens and encourages them, so that they too rise up and praise God.

35.14.3.en: 3- David's praise not only makes him feel his fellowship with the rest of his people, and makes his people feel him, but by praise he also joins a great people, not only on earth but also in heaven, namely the angels who praise God at all times.

35.14.4.en: 4- David's praise of God in the midst of the congregation shows David's faith and his boasting in glorifying the name of God; this not only encourages others to praise, but becomes a cause for receiving many blessings from God for the sake of his faith.

35.14.5.en: 5- The great congregation and the mighty people are a symbol of the entry of the Gentiles into the faith, and this is what happened in the Church of the New Testament, so that all praised God.

35.15.0.en: 19- Let not them that are mine enemies wrongfully rejoice over me: neither let them wink with the eye that hate me without a cause. 20- For they speak not peace: but they devise deceitful matters against them that are quiet in the land.

35.15.1.en: 21- Yea, they opened their mouth wide against me, and said, Aha, aha, our eye hath seen it.

35.15.2.en: Opened wide: opened their mouths in contempt and mockery.

35.15.4.en: 1- David asks God to rescue him from his enemies, so that they may not gloat over him by achieving their purposes and their injustice to him. What is meant is not only the earthly enemies, but even more the demons.

35.15.5.en: 2- The words of the verse (v. 19) were spoken by Christ Himself when He said, "But this cometh to pass, that the word might be fulfilled that is written in their law, They hated me without a cause" (Jn 15:25). So this verse is a clear prophecy of what happened in Christ.

35.15.6.en: 3- David also asked God to stop the hypocrisy and deceit of the enemies, who treated him with outward love but harbored evil toward him. So after acting out a deceitful love they wink with their eyes at one another, confirming their evil and their spite toward David.

35.15.7.en: 4- David's enemies want evil, and to create disturbances and anxiety, and they use every deceit or craft to achieve their aims, and they rejoice in harming the quiet and peaceful, like David.

35.15.8.en: 5- David's enemies express their hatred of him by mockery, ridicule and contempt, especially when they succeed in wronging him in any way. All this injustice David places before God to move Him to compassion, that He may deliver him from the hands of his enemies.

35.15.9.en: 6- The wicked used all their abilities for evil; they used their tongues, their thoughts, their mouths, their eyes and their hearts, and this means their being filled with evil and their complete subjection to Satan.

35.15.10.en: 7- These three verses apply to Christ, whom they mocked and insulted during His sufferings and crucifixion, and He endured all this out of love for us.

35.16.0.en: 22- This thou hast seen, O LORD: keep not silence: O Lord, be not far from me. 23- Stir up thyself, and awake to my judgment, even unto my cause, my God and my Lord. 24- Judge me, O LORD my God, according to thy righteousness; and let them not rejoice over me.

35.16.1.en: 25- Let them not say in their hearts, Ah, so would we have it: let them not say, We have swallowed him up.

35.16.2.en: 1- As David calls God to witness all the injustice that has befallen him, he implores Him not to be silent and not to be long-suffering any longer, because David is weary and needs God's swift intervention to rescue him. This shows the extent of David's suffering, and also the extent of his trust in God and his reliance on Him.

35.16.3.en: 2- The mighty David was able to turn the wrongs of others toward him into prayers and supplications to God, so he did not become angry with them or condemn them, but took refuge in God, and his love for Him increased.

35.16.4.en: 3- David trusts in God's power, but he sees God silent as though asleep, or heedless and not attentive to what is happening with David, so he presses Him to intervene. Here appears the importance of persistence in prayer - which God loves - because it is evidence of David's clinging to God alone to rescue him.

35.16.5.en: 4- David walks in uprightness, and his enemies wrong him; therefore he asks for God's justice, that God may judge and rule on his requests so as to remove the injustice from him. And everyone who walks in uprightness is a person who fears God and asks for God's intervention, and He rescues him and glorifies him.

35.16.6.en: 5- David also asks God to stop the mockery ("Aha") and the gloating of the enemies over him, because they thought they had deprived him of all ability, and fulfilled their desire by taking vengeance on him, so that he became like one dead in their sight, as though they had swallowed him; but despite David's apparent weakness before people, his heart was still strong, steadfast in the faith that God would intervene and rescue him.

35.16.7.en: 6- The Jews thought that they had got rid of Christ by His crucifixion and death, but David - in the spirit of prophecy - calls Christ to awake and rise from the dead, so that the demons see that His life was not swallowed up by death, but on the contrary He trampled death, and rose to give new life to all who believe in Him.

35.17.0.en: 26- Let them be ashamed and brought to confusion together that rejoice at mine hurt: let them be clothed with shame and dishonour that magnify themselves against me.

35.17.1.en: 1- God intervenes when David prays, and his enemies who gloat over him are turned to shame, because they see God's rescuing him and honoring him. And God allows them this shame as a chastening, that they may repent and know that God supports the righteous and shames the wicked.

35.17.2.en: 2- Shame and confusion cover the proud also, for pride is one of the chief characteristics of the wicked, while the humble God gives His peace and His joy.

35.18.0.en: 27- Let them shout for joy, and be glad, that favour my righteous cause: yea, let them say continually, Let the LORD be magnified, which hath pleasure in the prosperity of his servant.

35.18.1.en: 1- David implores God to gladden the hearts of the righteous, who wish for David's deliverance from his enemies, and then they glorify God and praise Him.

35.18.2.en: 2- This verse applies to Christ, who was in the form of shame when they insulted Him and crucified Him, and because He emptied Himself and became like a servant; but by His resurrection He declared His divinity and authority, and everyone who believed rejoiced in Him and enjoyed the blessings of salvation.

35.19.0.en: 28- And my tongue shall speak of thy righteousness and of thy praise all the day long.

35.19.1.en: 1- In the end, before the great works of God which David believed that God does with him, he thanked God and praised Him, and even kept praising Him all day long, that is, throughout his life.

35.19.2.en: 2- By the constant praise that extends all day long David means continuing in praise forever, where the day does not end in eternity, so that man lives in eternal joy.

35.19.3.en: 3- The stars praise God at all times without speaking, by their work, and so also man can praise throughout his life on earth, not only with words of praise, but by his faithfulness in the works he does for God's sake.

35.19.4.en: 4- As long as man's life has become praise, God in His fatherhood embraces him, defends him, and stands before his adversaries, that is, the demons and everyone who walks in evil, following the demons.

35.19.5.en: He that endureth to the end shall be saved; therefore continue in your prayers with persistence, confident of God's power, and He will reveal Himself to you and deliver you from all evil, and you will praise Him continually.

35.19.6.en: The works of the wicked and God's blessings to His children. To the chief Musician. By David the servant of the LORD. "The utterance of the transgression of the wicked" ... (v. 1) Introduction:

35.19.7.en: 1- Its author: David the prophet, who describes himself in the title as the servant of the Lord, and this means that the writer writes with authority from God, because he is His servant and near to Him, so he understands Him. The description "servant of the Lord" is repeated only in the eighteenth psalm.

35.19.8.en: 2- The psalm speaks of the characteristics of the wicked, meaning by this the wicked in general, and it may mean Saul specifically, because he did many evils against David.

35.19.9.en: 3- When it was written: David wrote it when he was being driven out by King Saul, or by Absalom.

35.19.10.en: 4- This psalm is divided into two parts, each the counterpart of the other; the first part is the first four verses, and it speaks of the wicked and their characteristics. The second part contains the rest of the psalm, and speaks of the characteristics of God, who is just, the Shepherd of His children, and the tender Father to whom His children make request, and He cares for them.

35.19.11.en: 5- This psalm establishes the faith of the children of God, for it lifts them up to contemplate His attributes, so they are not alarmed however much the wicked surround them, and they keep away from the wicked and hold fast to their life with God.

35.19.12.en: 6- This psalm is not found among the psalms in the Agpeya.
